column1: # Enumeration of properties of every one of the 82 canonical metric keys
# (ReflectionClass(MetricName::class)->getConstants(), MetricName being a plain
# final class with `public const string` members, not a backed enum) --
# measured for X11 step П3, whose ADR names the FINAL vocabulary for all 82
# keys, including the ones that are NOT renamed. This file only measures
# properties the decision leans on; it decides nothing and proposes no names.
# ROW COUNT: 82 data rows, one per MetricName constant. Verified identical to
# the kind=metric-key rows of docs/internal/plans/rule-vocabulary/enumeration-renames.tsv
# by: `awk -F'\t' '$2=="metric-key"{print $1}' enumeration-renames.tsv | sort`
# vs `php -r 'foreach ((new ReflectionClass(MetricName::class))->getConstants() as $v) echo $v."\n";' | sort`
# -- diff is empty (see REPORT below for the exact command run).
# HOW THIS WAS PRODUCED, column by column:
#  key/family/leaf -- key is one of the 82 MetricName::getConstants() values;
#    family is the substring before the first '.', leaf is everything after
#    it (`complexity.ccn` -> family `complexity`, leaf `ccn`;
#    `design.type-coverage.param.total` -> family `design`, leaf
#    `type-coverage.param.total`).
#  leaf_form/is_abbreviation/expanded_meaning -- CODE READING, not a
#    heuristic algorithm: each leaf was checked by hand against
#    src/Analysis/Evidence/Measurement/Contract/MetricName.php's own docblock,
#    the collector/rule docblocks that spell out the metric's name
#    (e.g. RfcCollector.php/RfcVisitor.php: "Collects RFC (Response for a
#    Class) metrics"; RFC has no website/docs/rules/coupling.md heading of its
#    own -- its only prose source is these two docblocks), `bin/qmx rules`
#    descriptions (e.g. "Checks Weighted Methods per Class (sum of method
#    complexities)" for complexity.wmc), and the website rule pages under
#    website/docs/rules/*.md (e.g. "## CBO -- Coupling Between Objects" style
#    headings). RULE APPLIED: is_abbreviation is "yes" iff the leaf's FIRST
#    dot/hyphen-separated token is one of the following, each with a source
#    citation for its expansion above (ccn, wmc -- website/docs/rules/complexity.md
#    headings; npath -- same page's "## NPath Complexity" heading + prose
#    "counts the total number of unique execution paths"; ca, ce, cbo --
#    src/Analysis/Evidence/Coupling/README.md's table; rfc -- RfcCollector.php/
#    RfcVisitor.php docblocks, no website heading; tcc, lcc, lcom --
#    website/docs/rules/cohesion.md headings; dit, noc, woc --
#    website/docs/rules/design*.md; mi -- website/docs/rules/maintainability.md;
#    loc, lloc, cloc -- src/Analysis/Evidence/Size/README.md). leaf_form
#    classifies the WHOLE leaf as `abbreviation` (leaf is exactly one such
#    token), `word` (a single ordinary English word, e.g. `cognitive`),
#    `word-phrase` (two or more ordinary words/flags, hyphen- or dot-joined,
#    none of them the leading abbreviation token), or `mixed` (an
#    abbreviation token combined with an ordinary word, e.g. `cbo-app`,
#    or a proper noun combined with a word, e.g. `halstead.volume` --
#    "Halstead" is the researcher's name (Halstead, 1977), neither a common
#    word nor an abbreviation). expanded_meaning is filled only when
#    is_abbreviation=yes, from the citation named above; empty for `word` and
#    for `mixed` leaves not led by the abbreviation token (their embedded
#    abbreviation, if any, is called out in `notes` instead, e.g.
#    code-smell.is-vo-constructor's "vo" = Value Object).
#  levels_published/aggregation_suffixes_published -- REFLECTION + CODE
#    READING. A PHP script (kept in scratch, not committed) boots the
#    production container via Infrastructure\DependencyInjection\ContainerFactory,
#    fetches the public AnalysisPipelineInterface service (the
#    MeasurementAggregationInterface alias itself is private and unreachable
#    from outside the container after compile), reflects into its private
#    `measurementAggregation` property, then into that service's private
#    `allDefinitions` array (list<MetricDefinition>, assembled from every
#    registered collector/derived-collector/global-collector in
#    MeasurementAggregationService's constructor -- see that class's own
#    `$this->allDefinitions = [...$regularDefinitions, ...$derivedDefinitions,
#    ...$this->globalDefinitions]`). For a key with a MetricDefinition (73 of
#    82), levels_published is the single `collectedAt` level: reading
#    ClassToNamespaceAggregator/NamespaceToProjectAggregator/
#    TreeAwareNamespaceAggregator/AggregationHelper::applyAggregations shows a
#    bare (unsuffixed) key is stored ONLY at its collection level -- every
#    aggregation target level stores a SUFFIXED name (base + '.' + strategy)
#    instead, never the bare key again. aggregation_suffixes_published is the
#    union, across every target level in `$definition->aggregations`, of the
#    declared AggregationStrategy values, PLUS an implicit `.count` wherever
#    `.avg` is declared without an explicit `.count` at that same level
#    (AggregationHelper::applyAggregations: "Auto-store count alongside
#    Average so higher levels know the sample size" -- read directly, not
#    inferred). 9 of the 82 keys have NO MetricDefinition at all (never touch
#    this reflection path) and were resolved by grepping every
#    `->with(MetricName::X` / `->withEntry(MetricName::X` call site by hand;
#    each gets a `notes` entry and is listed below under "WHAT THIS METHOD
#    DOES NOT SEE".
#  judged_by_channels/coincides_with_channel_code -- REFLECTION. A second PHP
#    script boots the same container, fetches
#    ChannelDeclarationRegistryInterface (public), calls staticDeclarations()
#    (the same oracle enumeration-renames.tsv's `channel` rows use), and for
#    every channel reflects its private ChannelDeclaration::$judges
#    (JudgedMetrics) down to the array of exact-spelling metric-key strings
#    it names (per ChannelDeclaration::judging()'s own docblock: "Keys are
#    declared in their exact published spelling, aggregate strategy
#    included: size.class-count is judged as size.class-count.sum"). The
#    per-key column lists every channel whose judged-key list contains this
#    key's EXACT bare string -- a channel that names only the `.sum`/`.max`/...
#    aggregate of a key (e.g. size.class-count is judged only as
#    size.class-count.sum) does NOT count as judging the bare key, and that
#    distinction is called out in `notes` for every row it affects.
#    coincides_with_channel_code is a plain set-membership check of the 82
#    keys against the 52 kind=channel rows of enumeration-renames.tsv.
#  user_addressable -- CODE READING of
#    src/Analysis/Evidence/ComputedMetrics/ComputedMetricFormulaValidator.php.
#    `validateMetricKeyExistence()` -> `assertKeyIsCatalogued()` ->
#    `existsInCatalog()` checks `MetricName::base($key)` (which strips a
#    trailing `.<AggregationStrategy>` suffix) against `catalogBaseKeys()`,
#    which reflects EVERY public constant of MetricName -- so a
#    `computed_metrics` formula may address any of the 82 base keys (or any
#    of their `.agg` suffix forms) as `m["<key>"]`, unconditionally, whether
#    or not that key is ever actually published at the level the formula
#    reads it from (the validator checks catalog membership, not runtime
#    presence -- a formula addressing a key nothing ever populates simply
#    reads null/0 at evaluation time). That half of the column is therefore
#    identical ("yes: computed_metrics") for all 82 rows by construction,
#    which is itself a measured fact, not an assumption; the TSV cell is kept
#    to that one short phrase (plus the threshold half below) per the task's
#    "yes/no + чем именно, коротко" -- the reasoning above lives here, not
#    repeated 82 times in the file. The second half, present only for the 18
#    keys with coincides_with_channel_code=yes, notes that a qmx.yaml/
#    `@qmx-threshold`/`--rule-opt` threshold can be written against this
#    literal because it doubles as a channel code -- corroborated by TWO
#    independent witnesses: the judges.json reflection (a channel's judged-key
#    list, cross-checked against `bin/qmx rules`' own printed text, which
#    lists each channel's `--rule-opt=<channel>:<option>=...` options under
#    that same literal) and MetricName.php's own docblock line
#    `@qmx-threshold coupling.cbo 73 -- ...`, which addresses the metric key
#    literally because it IS the channel code here. For a key that IS judged
#    but by a DIFFERENTLY-spelled channel (e.g. complexity.ccn, judged by
#    channel complexity.cyclomatic), the column says so explicitly: a user
#    cannot write a threshold against the literal "complexity.ccn" -- only
#    against "complexity.cyclomatic".
#  sites_* -- SLICES of the same-named columns already measured by
#    scripts/generate-rename-enumeration.php for this key's `metric-key` row
#    in enumeration-renames.tsv (whole-identifier match, word-boundary rule --
#    see that file's own header for the exact method). sites_docs = its
#    `website_docs` column. sites_config_presets = `presets` + `config`
#    summed. sites_total = the sum of ALL EIGHT of that file's occurrence
#    columns (src, tests, presets, config, baseline, website_docs,
#    benchmarks, finding_gate) -- wider than the four named sites_* slices,
#    which is why sites_total can exceed sites_src + sites_tests + sites_docs
#    + sites_config_presets (the difference is baseline + benchmarks +
#    finding_gate occurrences, not separately broken out here).
# WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE:
#  - The reflection path for levels_published/aggregation_suffixes_published
#    sees ONLY keys that flow through a registered MetricDefinition. 9 of the
#    82 keys never do, and were resolved by hand instead (grep, cited
#    file:line in each row's `notes`): complexity.wmc (synthesized in
#    CallableToClassAggregator.php:67 from the class-level sum of
#    complexity.ccn, written directly to the class bag, never aggregated
#    further -- levels_published=class only); size.symbol-method-count /
#    size.symbol-class-count (AggregationHelper::addSymbolCounts(), called
#    directly from CallableToClassAggregator.php (class, method-count only),
#    ClassToNamespaceAggregator.php / TreeAwareNamespaceAggregator.php
#    (namespace, both), and NamespaceToProjectAggregator.php (project, both));
#    security.hardcoded-credentials / security.sensitive-parameter (entry-type
#    DataBag-like MetricBag::withEntry() writes, one per detected occurrence,
#    at file level -- HardcodedCredentialsCollector.php,
#    SensitiveParameterCollector.php); code-smell.unused-private.{total,
#    method,property,constant} (UnusedPrivateCollector::getMetricDefinitions()
#    literally `return [];` -- published instead through
#    ClassMetricsProviderInterface at class level, UnusedPrivateCollector.php).
#    A key outside this list of 9 that this method still could not resolve
#    would show levels_published=unknown; none did -- every one of the 82 was
#    resolved by one of the two methods.
#  - The reflection path also cannot see a GlobalContextCollector writing a
#    BARE key directly at a level beyond its MetricDefinition's `collectedAt`,
#    bypassing the generic aggregation pipeline entirely -- found once, by
#    hand, in CouplingCollector.php: computeNamespaceMetrics() (lines
#    268-293) recomputes ca/ce/cbo/instability straight from the dependency
#    graph and writes them bare at NAMESPACE level, alongside (not instead
#    of) the aggregated .sum/.avg/.max/.p95 forms the same MetricDefinition
#    publishes at that level from rolling up class values -- two different
#    numbers under the base spelling and the suffixed spelling respectively.
#    This was caught only by manually reading every GlobalContextCollector
#    (6 of them) for repository->add()/->addScalar() calls beyond what
#    getMetricDefinitions() declares; the other 5 (NocCollector,
#    DitGlobalCollector, ClassRankCollector, DistanceCollector,
#    AbstractnessCollector) write only their declared single level.
#    DitGlobalCollector looks similar (it also writes design.dit) but is NOT
#    a second level -- its own docblock says it "overwrites with correct
#    cross-file values" at the SAME class level InheritanceDepthCollector
#    already declared, and its getMetricDefinitions() deliberately returns
#    `[]` to avoid a duplicate declaration. A systematic sweep for this
#    pattern across every collector (not just the 82 keys already flagged
#    here) was not run; it would be
#    `grep -rn "addScalar(\|MetricBag())->with(" src/Analysis/Evidence/*/*.php`
#    followed by comparing each write site's level against its
#    MetricDefinition's collectedAt/aggregations, collector by collector.
#  - Two more literal-key writer patterns were seen and are named, not
#    measured further: (a) `MetricName::X . ':' . $classFqn` -- RfcCollector.php
#    lines 90-92 and UnusedPrivateCollector::addClassMetrics() write a
#    colon-suffixed variant of a MetricName literal into an intermediate
#    per-file bag before the class-level bag is built; whether this
#    colon-suffixed form ever reaches a published report was not checked here
#    (the cheap check would be `grep -c ':' ` against a structurally-parsed
#    report dump, the way enumeration-metric-key-spellings.tsv did it for the
#    prior rename). (b) `DataBag` (src/Analysis/Evidence/Measurement/DataBag.php)
#    is a second, separate keyed-entry container (occurrences/findings, not
#    metrics) some collectors use instead of MetricBag; it was not inventoried
#    here beyond noting that it exists and is a distinct namespace of keys
#    from the one this file measures.
#  - judged_by_channels/coincides_with_channel_code see only the STATIC
#    per-rule channel declarations (staticDeclarations()), by the same
#    construction enumeration-renames.tsv's channel rows use -- the run-time
#    `computed.*`/`health.*` family is excluded by that method on purpose (no
#    fixed set to enumerate; see ChannelDeclarationRegistryInterface's own
#    docblock) and cannot judge a MetricName key by definition (a computed
#    metric's formula READS catalog keys, its channel does not JUDGE one).
#    ADR 0046 also names six channels a related check does not cover; this
#    column does not re-derive that list, it only reads what `$judges`
#    already carries for the 52 statically-declared channels.
#  - user_addressable's `computed_metrics` half is a SYNTACTIC validator
#    check (catalog membership), not a runtime-presence check: it says a
#    formula MAY reference the key, not that the key WILL ever be non-null
#    for every level the formula is defined at. Whether a specific formula
#    misses at a specific level is a per-formula runtime question this
#    column does not answer.
#  - CLI/qmx.yaml threshold addressability was measured only through the
#    literal-coincidence test (does the key spell a channel code exactly).
#    A metric judged by a same-family but differently-spelled channel (e.g.
#    complexity.ccn / complexity.cyclomatic) DOES have a working threshold
#    path, just not one spelled with this key's own literal; that is called
#    out per-row rather than counted as "no" outright.
# ARE THERE PUBLISHED METRIC KEYS OUTSIDE MetricName? YES -- MEASURED FROM
# TWO INDEPENDENT WITNESSES, WRITE SIDE AND READ SIDE, THAT AGREE:
#  WITNESS 1 (write side): `grep -rnE "->with\('[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*'|
#  ->withEntry\('[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*'" src/ | grep -v "MetricName::"` finds
#  every MetricBag write keyed by a string literal instead of a MetricName::
#  constant reference, then excludes the ones whose literal is merely a
#  re-spelling of an existing MetricName value (e.g.
#  CyclomaticComplexityVisitor.php:93 writes 'complexity.ccn' as a literal,
#  but that string IS MetricName::COMPLEXITY_CCN's value). Two scalar-shaped
#  survivors are NOT declared anywhere in MetricName.php:
#    - `npath-complexity.factors` (NpathComplexityVisitor.php:133)
#    - `cognitive-complexity.increments` (CognitiveComplexityVisitor.php:136)
#  A companion check, `grep -rnE "const [A-Za-z_]+ = '[a-z][a-z-]*(\.[a-z][a-z-]*)+'"
#  src/Analysis/Evidence | grep -v Contract/MetricName.php`, looked for a
#  private collector-owned constant holding a dotted metric-like literal the
#  way the pre-X10 vocabulary used to (see
#  enumeration-metric-key-spellings.tsv's own "local collector-owned literals"
#  paragraph) -- empty result: no such constant remains today.
#  WITNESS 2 (read side), which turned up a THIRD, WIDER pattern the write-side
#  grep's `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]*` character class cannot match at all because these
#  keys are built by RUNTIME STRING INTERPOLATION, not a literal:
#  `grep -rn "->entries(" src/ | grep -v Contract/` lists every call that reads
#  a MetricBag/DataBag entry list back, i.e. every key some producer actually
#  publishes as consumable data. Four call sites read an INTERPOLATED key that
#  can never appear in MetricName.php by construction:
#    - `$metrics->entries("security.{$type}")` (AbstractSecurityPatternRule.php:125)
#      -- PATTERN_TYPE is 'command_injection'/'sql_injection'/'xss' per
#      concrete rule subclass, giving `security.command_injection`,
#      `security.sql_injection`, `security.xss` (snake_case types under a
#      dot, not the kebab-case MetricName convention; NOT the same string as
#      the channel codes security.command-injection/security.sql-injection/
#      security.xss, which use hyphens)
#    - `$metrics->entries("codeSmell.{$type}")` (AbstractCodeSmellRule.php:126)
#      -- SMELL_TYPE per subclass (boolean_argument, count_in_loop,
#      debug_code, empty_catch, eval, exit, goto, error_suppression,
#      superglobals), giving `codeSmell.boolean_argument` etc. -- a THIRD
#      spelling convention (camelCase family + snake_case type) coexisting
#      with MetricName's kebab-case `code-smell.*` and the channel registry's
#      kebab-case `code-smell.*` channel codes; none of these codeSmell.*
#      strings is a MetricName constant, a channel code, or reachable through
#      `MetricName::base()`
#    - `$metrics->entries("identicalSubExpression.{$type}")`
#      (IdenticalSubExpressionRule.php:96) -- same camelCase-family pattern,
#      keyed by IdenticalSubExpressionCollector's own finding-type strings
#    - `$metrics->entries($entryKey)` (UnusedPrivateRule.php:93) -- reads back
#      the ENTRY_METHOD/ENTRY_PROPERTY/ENTRY_CONSTANT literals, which for this
#      one call site DO happen to be MetricName constants (see the 82-key
#      table's code-smell.unused-private.{method,property,constant} rows) --
#      named here only to show the read-side grep does not uniformly mean
#      "outside MetricName": each hit was checked individually.
#  CROSS-CHECK, the "two witnesses" the task asked for: 73 of the 82
#  MetricName constants have a MetricDefinition (measured for
#  levels_published above); the other 9 do not, and BOTH the write-side and
#  read-side greps independently converge on a published spelling for every
#  one of those 9 without finding a 10th uncatalogued scalar key -- i.e. the
#  MetricDefinition-shaped 73 + the by-hand 9 is exactly a bijection onto the
#  82 constants, which is itself evidence the *scalar* catalog is complete.
#  The camelCase/snake_case entry families above are a DIFFERENT thing: they
#  are occurrence-shaped diagnostic breakdown data (which decision point, at
#  which line, contributed how much), consumed only by their own rule's
#  finding message, not scalar catalog metrics a report's top-level "metrics"
#  object lists keyed by a MetricName constant -- but they ARE real, currently
#  published MetricBag/DataBag content that MetricName's 82-constant
#  enumeration does not, and structurally cannot, see. An ADR relying on "the
#  82-key universe is everything this product publishes" should read this as
#  the measured exception, not as a claim that no such exception exists: at
#  least three more spelling FAMILIES (security.<snake_case>,
#  codeSmell.<snake_case>, identicalSubExpression.<snake_case>) live entirely
#  outside the 82-key, kebab-case vocabulary this file enumerates.
